name: mindplan-mcp

tools.name: run_check
tools.description: Call before in-review, before ship, and before telling the user the work is done. Runs the same check as `mindplan-mcp check` (graph load, exclusivity, coverage, presence, leftovers, import matrix); warnings never fail it. Compact by default: { ok, counts, failures, warnings: [{ id, text }], info, acknowledged, unchanged }, listing only warnings not shown earlier in this session or acknowledged (acknowledge_warning); nodes lists those nodes' warnings again; compact: false returns the CLI output. A graph that needs setup_project or upgrade_project fails with Blocked: Version. An unclaimed source file is Blocked: Coverage with its probable owner and the claim call, or leads with create_node when no node has a file in its folder. Pass change to also run the in-review gate on every member of that change. Pass merge before telling the user a PR is ready to merge: it Blocks nodes still in review, and shipped nodes with no open revision whose claimed files changed against base while their territory did not (open_next + ship, or patch_node_territory in place); "strict" also Blocks in-progress nodes whose claimed files changed. Pass after_merge after merging a branch that changed the graph. Pass run_tests (with change or nodes) to run their linked tests; passing tests close each node's verify item. Details: get_spec({ topic: "run_check" }).

base.description: Opt-in: also enforce dirty-src ownership against this git ref (not used by CI).

change.description: Also check every member of this change (imports, ownership, stale text) and list its members, each with kind revision | planned.

merge.description: Merge gate: true Blocks in-review nodes and Bugs; "strict" also Blocks in-progress nodes whose claimed files changed against base (default: the main/master merge base).

after_merge.description: After merging a branch that changed mindplan/: also Block git conflict markers, a node id in two folders, a decision id in two files, a tracked mindplan/map.md, and a missing or behind version.json; a revision whose base no longer matches live is a Warning: after-merge: (fix: rebase_revision).

compact.description: Default true: counts, info, and only new warnings with ids. false: the full output, every warning as text, and info.

nodes.description: Limit warnings to these nodes; failures stay graph-wide, and counts.out_of_scope says how many warnings were left out. With run_tests: the nodes whose linked tests run.

run_tests.description: Also run the linked tests of change's members (or of nodes) with config tests.command; a failure is Blocked: Tests. Passing tests close each node's default verify item; spec and impl close at ship.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: get_drift
tools.description: Call when a reply's drift count says source files drift and you need every path, or before handing off. Returns { count, paths: [{ path, class, owner_id?, state?, next_state? }], expected, reminder }: every uncommitted source file whose owner has no open update (owner_idle), that a node claims but is missing (claimed_missing), or that no node claims (unowned). Other replies carry only drift: { count, new_since_last_reply }. Details: get_spec({ topic: "get_drift" }).

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: acknowledge_warning
tools.description: Call when a run_check warning is known and accepted, so compact checks stop listing it. Stores the w- ids a compact run_check lists in .mindplan-cache/acks.json of this root (no graph write); returns { acknowledged: [ids] }. A warning whose text changes gets a new id and shows again. Details: get_spec({ topic: "acknowledge_warning" }).

id.description: One warning id (w-<10 hex>) from a compact run_check.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: get_mindplan_graph
tools.description: Call when you need the graph's nodes and edges, or a slice of them; prefer orient_for_work for one piece of work. Returns one page: nodes sorted by id, the edges whose source is in the page, totals, and next_offset while nodes remain (up to 200 nodes per page). Filter with state / type / change (AND across, OR within an array), project with fields, and drop or narrow edges with edges: e.g. state: ["draft", "ready"], fields: ["id", "type", "title", "change"], edges: false lists what is planned but not built. Details: get_spec({ topic: "get_mindplan_graph" }).

state.description: Only nodes in this state, or in any of these states (e.g. "ready", ["in-progress", "in-review"]). Matches the live state field.

type.description: Only nodes of this type, or of any of these types.

change.description: Only the nodes of this change: the nodes holding an open revision of it, and pre-ship nodes whose change field it is.

fields.description: Node fields to return (id is always included), e.g. ["id", "type", "title", "change"]. Valid: id, type, title, description, state, created_at, updated_at, shipped_at, revisions, split_at, split_into, churn, churn_behavior, churn_wiring, churn_at, severity, belongs_to, depends_on, exposes, leads_to, mounts, affects, implements, added_claims, tests, aliases, planned, attributed, role, next, open_revisions, rules, change, change_ref, decisions.

edges.description: true (default): every edge whose source is in the page. false: no edges and no total_edges. An array: only edges of those types (OR); total_edges counts them. Valid types: depends_on, belongs_to, exposes, leads_to, affects, mounts.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: export_mindplan_view
tools.description: Call when a human wants a map for a PR or a doc (agents orient with find_related_nodes). Exports the typed DAG as Mermaid or DOT: the full filtered map, or with focus that node and its 1-hop neighborhood; retired nodes and closed bugs are hidden by default. A diagram over 80000 characters is Blocked unless you pass focus or output (a repo-relative file path, outside mindplan/). Details: get_spec({ topic: "export_mindplan_view" }).

focus.description: When set, export focus + 1-hop linked neighborhood only.

include_retired.description: Include deprecated/cancelled nodes and closed bugs (resolved/wontfix). Default false.

decisions.description: Label each node that has active decisions with their count. Default false.

output.description: Repo-relative file path to write the diagram to (outside mindplan/). The result then carries written_to and no diagram.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: find_related_nodes
tools.description: Call before creating a node, to reuse one that already exists. Ranks nodes for a text query (keyword plus semantic; an exact id ranks first) and returns the focus node plus its 1-hop neighborhood as summaries. Pass query and/or node_id; get_node_context reads full territory. Details: get_spec({ topic: "find_related_nodes" }).

query.description: Free-text query to rank nodes (keyword and semantic: id, title, description, area, headings, paths). Required if node_id omitted.

node_id.description: Force focus to this node when present. Required if query is empty.

type.description: Optional type filter applied before ranking.

limit.description: Max ranked matches to return (default 5, max 20).

area.description: A Capability id (list_areas): rank only that Capability's Interactions, the Interfaces exposing them, and the Foundations they depend on. Omit for a question that cuts across Capabilities.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: list_areas
tools.description: Call when you are unsure where work lands. Returns every Capability as one compact table row (id, title, short description, interaction / interface / foundation counts, open_bugs); pass a row's id as area to orient_for_work or find_related_nodes. Details: get_spec({ topic: "list_areas" }).

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: get_node_implementation
tools.description: Call before editing a file, to see which node owns it, or to list a node's claimed files. Pass node_id for its implements files ({ path, exists }, next_files?), or path for the owner of that path. Details: get_spec({ topic: "get_node_implementation" }).

node_id.description: Node id whose implements list to read. Required unless path is set.

path.description: Repo-relative path to look up owner for.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: get_node_context
tools.description: Call when you are about to read or edit one node's territory. Returns its record, body (without ## Rules / ## Decisions), own rules, active decisions, resolved_rules (sources past distance 1 as one line unless include_inherited_rules; text this session already received as { node_id, version, unchanged: true }), and attachments, plus the next slot while a revision is open; it counts as orienting on the node. With several open revisions pass change to read one (otherwise only live comes back). slot or section returns only that body part, the minimal record (id, type, state, title), the rules, and decisions not yet sent; include_superseded and include_inherited_decisions widen the decisions. To find exact text for a replace edit use find_in_node. Details: get_spec({ topic: "get_node_context" }).

node_id.description: The id of the node whose territory to read.

include_superseded.description: Also return superseded decisions (each names superseded_by). Default false.

include_inherited_decisions.description: Also return the decisions inherited through belongs_to / depends_on (a Bug: past the nodes it affects): whole at distance 1, one line { id, node_id, distance, decision } beyond. Default false: only their count and nodes.

include_inherited_rules.description: Also return the text of rules from sources past distance 1 (a Foundation's Foundations, a Capability's further links). Default false: those come back as one line { node_id, distance, version, first, count }.

slot.description: Return only this slot's body (get_node_context: and its decisions): current (live) or next (the open revision; Blocked when none is open).

section.description: Return only this section of each body, e.g. "## Spec"; a missing heading is Blocked and lists the sections. Read a large node a section at a time.

change.description: Which open revision of the node (its change id). May be omitted when the node has at most one open revision.

resend_rules.description: Return every rule text again, even text this session already received (default false: a source whose text already reached you comes back as { node_id, version, unchanged: true }). Use after a context summary.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: find_in_node
tools.description: Call when you need the exact text of a node for patch_node_territory's replace edit. Searches the node's body as replace.find sees it (live without ## Rules / ## Decisions, plus the open revision) and returns each matching line with its slot, line, section, and a snippet of whole lines that occurs exactly once in that slot: pass it as replace.find (with the match's slot and change). Details: get_spec({ topic: "find_in_node" }).

node_id.description: The node whose body to search.

text.description: The text to find, matched line by line: a case-insensitive substring unless case_sensitive or regex.

slot.description: current (live) or next (an open revision; Blocked when none is open). Default: live, plus the open revision change names or the only open one.

change.description: Which open revision of the node (its change id). May be omitted when the node has at most one open revision.

regex.description: Treat text as a JavaScript regular expression (Blocked when invalid). Default false.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: search_graph
tools.description: Call when you need to know which nodes' text mentions something (a path, a term, a phrase) instead of grepping mindplan/. Searches the body of every non-retired node (live and each open revision) and returns matching lines { node_id, type, slot, change?, line, section, match }. find_in_node then gives a replace-ready snippet. Details: get_spec({ topic: "search_graph" }).

text.description: The text to find, matched line by line: a case-insensitive substring unless case_sensitive or regex.

regex.description: Treat text as a JavaScript regular expression (Blocked when invalid). Default false.

type.description: Only search nodes of this type.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: orient_for_work
tools.description: Call before working on a node: a write on a node is Blocked: Orientation until that node had a full reply in this session, and again after the rules reaching it changed (create_node never is). With query alone it returns ranked rows (a clear winner comes back in full with auto_focus: true); with node_id, the node: record, active-slot body, owned files, shape, its mandatory node rules (its own and those at distance 1 in full, further sources as one line), and its decisions; depth full adds the neighborhood, blast radius, and stability. change alone orients on every member of a change and clears the gate for all of them; with node_id it reads that node's revision. node_ids orients on several nodes in one lean reply. Rule text this session already received comes back as { node_id, version, unchanged: true } (resend_rules returns it again); known_rules_versions also leaves out text you hold; a reply without the rules section does not clear the gate. slot or section returns only that body part plus the minimal record. Replies that orient carry project_rules when the project rules have not reached the session or changed. Details: get_spec({ topic: "orient_for_work" }).

query.description: Free-text query to rank nodes. Required if node_id and change are omitted.

node_id.description: Force focus to this node when present.

node_ids.description: Orient on several nodes in one call (alone, without query, node_id, or change): each node lean (id, type, state, title, revisions, rules_from, decision count) and every rule source once. Clears the write gate for all of them.

change.description: Alone: orient on every member of this change (each node's revision of it, planned sources, and nodes holding a decision under it) in one reply. With node_id: read that node's open revision of this change.

limit.description: Max ranked rows (default 8 for a query alone, 5 with node_id).

depth.description: rules: the node's rules and record only. body (default): also its body and files. full: also the neighborhood, blast radius, and stability.

include_superseded.description: Also return superseded decisions in the decisions block (each names superseded_by). Default false.

include_inherited_decisions.description: Also return the decisions inherited through belongs_to / depends_on (a Bug: past the nodes it affects): whole at distance 1, one line { id, node_id, distance, decision } beyond. Default false: only their count and nodes.

include_inherited_rules.description: Also return the text of rules from sources past distance 1 (a Foundation's Foundations, a Capability's further links). Default false: those come back as one line { node_id, distance, version, first, count }.

known_rules_versions.description: Node id → rules version you already hold (from an earlier rules block); those entries come back without their text, with unchanged: true.

area.description: A Capability id (list_areas): rank only that Capability's Interactions, the Interfaces exposing them, and the Foundations they depend on. Omit for a question that cuts across Capabilities.

slot.description: Return only this slot's body (get_node_context: and its decisions): current (live) or next (the open revision; Blocked when none is open).

section.description: Return only this section of each body, e.g. "## Spec"; a missing heading is Blocked and lists the sections. Read a large node a section at a time.

resend_rules.description: Return every rule text again, even text this session already received (default false: a source whose text already reached you comes back as { node_id, version, unchanged: true }). Use after a context summary.

sections.description: Return only these parts (plus focus and query): rules, decisions, record, body, files, shape, revisions, open_items, blast_radius, stability, neighborhood, drift. A reply without "rules" does not clear the write gate. "drift" returns the full drift list (otherwise drift is { count, new_since_last_reply }). Default: every part depth returns.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: next_page
tools.description: Call when a reply carries truncated: [{ path, shown, total, cursor }] and you need more of that list. Returns { path, from, items, total, next_cursor? }: the next items that fit the reply budget; pass next_cursor for more. Cursors live for this session. Details: get_spec({ topic: "next_page" }).

cursor.description: A cursor from a reply's truncated list, or a next_cursor.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Call before the first answer or code change in a session, and again after the product description or rules change. Returns the MindPlan playbook and this product's description and rules ({ path, description, rules, rules_version, playbook, check, version?, restart? }). version appears only when the graph needs setup_project, upgrade_project, or a newer server; until then other graph tools are Blocked. restart means a different mindplan-mcp was installed under this server: have the user restart it, then call again. Details: get_spec({ topic: "get_project" }).

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Call when the server seems slow, attached to the wrong folder, or a graph tool fails in a way the message does not explain. Returns the server and Node versions, the project root it serves, the graph's state (setup, upgrade, server-behind, current), graph-load time through the cache (load_error says why it did not load), and which derived caches exist. Answers in every graph state. Details: get_spec({ topic: "doctor" }).

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: get_spec
tools.description: Call when you need a specific MindPlan rule (lifecycle, required sections, change ids, decisions, orientation) instead of guessing or retrying. Returns one part of the running server's SPEC.md ({ topic, version, text }) by topic id, or a tool's entry by tool name; without topic it lists them. Details: get_spec({ topic: "get_spec" }).

topic.description: A topic id (e.g. territory-shape, lifecycle, change-ids, neighbors, decisions) or a tool name (e.g. run_check). Omit to list them.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Call when the playbook or the server instructions name a skill, before acting on it. Returns { name, text, files } (text is SKILL.md without frontmatter); pass file to read one supporting file; without name it lists the skills. Details: get_spec({ topic: "get_skill" }).

name.description: Skill name, e.g. plan-project or define-entities. Omit to list them.

file.description: A supporting file of the skill, as listed in files (e.g. examples.md). Needs name.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: get_rules
tools.description: Call to re-read the project rules explicitly: after a context summary, or when a rules push was missed. Returns the mandatory project rules ({ path, rules, rules_version }) from mindplan/project.md and records them as served to this session. Pass known_version only while you still hold that text; unchanged: true means it still applies. Node rules arrive through orient_for_work. Details: get_spec({ topic: "get_rules" }).

known_version.description: The rules_version of rules text you still hold (from get_project or get_rules); the text is left out when it still matches. Omit it when you no longer have the text.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: patch_node_territory
tools.description: Call when a node's title, description, or body should match the work, before the feature code. The writer for territory prose (never edit mindplan/ with host file tools): body (whole), section + text (one ## section), replace { find, with }, toggle_checkboxes, add_checklist_items, title / description / role. On a shipped node it writes the open revision (change picks one when several are open; with none it is Blocked: edit the code in place). Otherwise change sets the node's change id. aliases replaces search aliases on any node, live. A contract write to a slot in state ready (territory text or checkboxes, claims, links) moves that slot back to draft and returns readiness_reset; self-ready it again after review. Details: get_spec({ topic: "patch_node_territory" }).

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: Node whose territory to patch.

aliases.description: Search aliases: synonyms, the words users will say, other languages (e.g. quote, request a quote, ofertă). Replaces the list; [] clears it. At most 20, each up to 60 characters.

body.description: Replace entire territory body below frontmatter.

section.description: Heading of one section to rewrite, e.g. "## Purpose". Needs text. Other sections and the heading line stay as they are.

text.description: Replacement text for the section named by section.

replace.description: Replace one exact piece of the body without resending it.

find.description: Exact text to find in the body (must be unique unless all).

toggle_checkboxes.description: Tick or untick Atomic Ops / Checklist items by id or exact text. Returns toggled: the lines as written. Close an item honestly with note or not_applicable instead of rewording it.

id.description: The item's id: its "{#id}" tag (defaults: spec, impl, verify).

contains.description: The item's full text, tag and annotation excluded (exact match; a substring is Blocked). Pass id or contains.

checked.description: true for [x], false for [ ]. Optional with note or not_applicable (both tick).

all.description: Toggle every item with that exact text. Without it, text matching several items is Blocked.

note.description: Tick with a note, written as " — note: <text>" after the item.

not_applicable.description: Tick as not applicable with a reason, written as " — n/a: <reason>". Counts as done.

add_checklist_items.description: Append unticked items to the slot's Atomic Ops, tagged {#id kind}. A review or deploy item waits on people: it does not hold up dependents once the node is in-review with every build item ticked, but the node ships only when it is ticked.

text.description: The item's wording (no tag or annotation).

id.description: A lowercase slug, unique in the slot.

kind.description: Who closes it: build (default; the agent), review or deploy (a person).

change.description: On a shipped node with open revisions: which revision to patch (may be omitted when only one is open). Otherwise: set the node's change id (a slug); empty string clears it. Blocked on a shipped node with no open next.

change_ref.description: Optional branch name or PR URL for the change. Empty string clears it.

slot.description: Territory slot to patch: next is the open revision (picked by change). Defaults to next when a revision is open.

split_into.description: Foundation with an open revision only: the Foundations this revision splits out of it. Shipping the revision records the split (split_at, split_into) for those it depends_on, and resets its hotspot rate.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: confirm_territory
tools.description: Call when the merge gate Blocks a shipped node whose claimed files changed but whose territory did not, and its text still describes the code (a removed script, a bumped constant): records who confirmed it, why, and each file's content hash in the node's confirmed.json, so the gate passes it without a made-up prose edit. Editing a confirmed file again Blocks again. A changed contract needs open_next and ship instead; stale text needs patch_node_territory. Only a shipped node with no open revision. Details: get_spec({ topic: "confirm_territory" }).

node_id.description: Shipped Foundation, Interaction, or Interface with no open revision.

files.description: Project-relative files to confirm, each claimed by the node (default: its claimed files changed against the default branch, as the merge gate counts them).

note.description: One line: why the node's text still describes the changed files.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: patch_node_rules
tools.description: Call when a rule applies to one node and the work that inherits from it, not everywhere (patch_project_rules covers that). Replaces the node's ## Rules section (empty string clears it), shipped nodes included, without open_next. Returns rules_impact: the nodes the rules reach. Details: get_spec({ topic: "patch_node_rules" }).

node_id.description: Node whose rules to replace.

rules.description: Replace the node's ## Rules section. Empty string clears it. No level-1 or level-2 headings.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: record_decision
tools.description: Call when you choose between viable designs (a data shape, an ordering guarantee, which system owns a fact), on the node the choice shapes. Writes decisions/<id>.md in the node's open revision of change (or its only one), else beside live; list every other node it shapes in nodes. Never rewritten: to change one, record a new decision with supersedes. A decision-worthy revision is Blocked at in-review until a decision is recorded under its change. Never resets readiness. Details: get_spec({ topic: "record_decision" }).

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: Node the decision shapes (not a Bug).

alternatives.description: What else was considered, one line each (the alternative you rejected, and why it lost).

why.description: The constraint or trade-off that decided it.

consequences.description: What this makes harder or forbids.

keep_whole.description: The node stays one node on purpose (e.g. auth): hotspot detection skips it until this decision is superseded.

supersedes.description: Id of an active decision on this node, its Capability, or its Foundations that this one replaces.

change.description: Which open revision of the node to record it in, and the change id it is tagged with (default: the node's only open revision's change; required when several are open). A change the node has no revision of only tags the decision, written live: the node's own change id is never set, so a decision alone does not make a shipped node a member of the change.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. d-capacity-on-booking. Generated from the decision when omitted.

nodes.description: Every node this one decision shapes (none a Bug). It clears the decision gate of their revisions under the same change, or any change when untagged.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: list_decisions
tools.description: Call before reshaping a design someone else chose, or to read the reasoning trail of a node or change. Returns { decisions, count } for one node, one change, or the whole graph, each with its node, status, and superseded_by; superseded entries only with include_superseded. Details: get_spec({ topic: "list_decisions" }).

node_id.description: List this node's own decisions.

change.description: List decisions recorded under this change id.

include_superseded.description: Also return superseded decisions. Default false.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: patch_project_description
tools.description: Call when the product summary changes. The next session start calls get_project again. Writes the ## Description section of mindplan/project.md via the territory store. Leaves ## Rules unchanged. Do not hand-edit project.md.

description.description: Replace the ## Description section body. Empty string clears it.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: patch_project_rules
tools.description: Call when a standing rule for all work changes; a rule about one node's work belongs in patch_node_rules instead. Writes the ## Rules section of mindplan/project.md (## Description unchanged; do not hand-edit it): add / remove change single rules, rules replaces the whole text. Rules reach a session once, through get_project, get_rules, or the project_rules push in orient replies; write tools are Blocked: Rules until they have. Returns a confirmation ({ rules_version, count, added, removed, skipped? }), not the rules; get_rules returns the text. Details: get_spec({ topic: "patch_project_rules" }).

rules.description: Replace the whole ## Rules section body. Empty string clears it. Not combined with add / remove.

add.description: Rules to append, each as one bullet. A rule already present is skipped.

remove.description: Rules to drop, by their text (the full rule, or a fragment that matches exactly one). No match or several is Blocked. Applied before add.

root.description: Absolute path to a checkout or git worktree whose mindplan/ this call reads and writes. Default: the server's project root.

tools.name: patch_config
tools.description: Call when source roots, exclude paths, decision-gate settings, hotspot thresholds, the fan-out threshold, search, reply size, the test command, or when rules' command checks run change. Writes mindplan/config.json sources, exclude, decisions, hotspots, fan_out, fan_in, search, replies, tests, and/or rule_checks via the territory store. Do not hand-edit config.json.

sources.description: Glob list for the ownership universe (replaces sources when set).

exclude.description: Glob list excluded from the universe (replaces exclude when set).

decisions.description: Decision-gate settings. A field not passed keeps its stored value.

tools.name: set_implementation_files
tools.description: Call before writing a file the node does not yet claim. Changes the server-owned implements list of a Foundation, Interaction, or Interface: add (default) and remove entries; files replaces the whole list only with replace: true. Entries are files, directories ending in /, or globs (* ** ?). Pre-ship writes current; with an open revision it writes a delta (change picks the revision when several are open). A shipped node with no open revision may only add exact files in a folder it already dominates (listed in added_in_place: name each in the body with patch_node_territory); removing, globbing, claiming elsewhere, or claiming a migration or schema file is Blocked → open_next. Ownership conflicts are rejected. attributed lists files this revision adds in another node's claimed folder: that node keeps ownership, the decision gate and blast radius count them here. A contract write to a slot in state ready (territory text or checkboxes, claims, links) moves that slot back to draft and returns readiness_reset; self-ready it again after review. Details: get_spec({ topic: "set_implementation_files" }).

tools.name: link_nodes

On a shipped node with an open revision the edge goes to it as a delta (change picks the revision when several are open); with change and no open revision of it, the edge is planned under that change (live graph unchanged; applied when open_next opens the node with that change). A contract write to a slot in state ready (territory text or checkboxes, claims, links) moves that slot back to draft and returns readiness_reset; self-ready it again after review. Details: get_spec({ topic: "link_nodes" }).

tools.name: open_next
tools.description: Call when a shipped node's contract changes, before editing that contract. Opens a draft revision under change (required) while the live node keeps serving; a node may hold several, one per change. Optional title/description overrides. Ship it with update_node_status (pass change when several are open) or abandon it with discard_next; shipping one rebases its siblings (conflicts go to resolve_conflict). Blocked when the node is not shipped or already has that change open. reason (required) says why: behavior, wiring, fix, platform, text, or refactor; only behavior and wiring count toward the node's hotspot rate. On a hotspot the result carries the diagnosis (invert or split) and a decision_prompt: do that refactor (a revision with reason refactor), or record why not. Details: get_spec({ topic: "open_next" }).

tools.name: update_node_status
tools.description: Call when a node should move along the build or bug pipeline, including ship or resolved at handoff. Build: draft -> ready -> in-progress -> in-review -> ship (stable/unstable computed). Bug: open -> triaged -> fixing -> in-review -> resolved | wontfix. Three forms: node_id + new_status (one node; on a shipped node it moves one open revision, pass change when it has several); revisions: [...] (a batch, each item tried in order; when only some moved the result has partial: true and blocked_count, so check it); scope + new_status (all_open_updates, node_and_dependents, or change; validated before the first write; dry_run previews). To ship a change in one call: update_node_status({ scope: "change", change, new_status: "ship" }); nodes: [...] limits it to those members. A scoped walk is all-or-nothing unless skip_blocked: true; walking to ship past a node's in-review stop needs skip_review: true. Other scopes leave a node with several open revisions in needs_change_walk. Ship writes the revision over live and rebases its siblings; a revision with conflicts is Blocked at in-review and ship until resolve_conflict clears them. Moves to in-review and ship run the check's import and ownership rules; a decision-worthy revision with no decision recorded is Blocked: Decision (record_decision). Details: get_spec({ topic: "update_node_status" }).

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: The id of the single node to transition. Mutually exclusive with revisions.

new_status.description: Foundation/Interaction/Interface: draft | ready | in-progress | in-review | ship | cancelled | deprecated. Bug: open | triaged | fixing | in-review | resolved | wontfix. From stable/unstable: deprecated only (or open_next then build/ship the revision). Pre-ship abandon: cancelled from draft|ready|in-progress|in-review. Required with node_id. Omit when using revisions.

scope.description: Walk many nodes in one call to the new_status target: all_open_updates (every shipped node with an open revision, and every pre-ship node being built: in-progress or in-review; draft and ready plans are never walked) or node_and_dependents (node_id plus its open dependents), or change (every open revision with that change id, draft and ready included). The server orders Foundations, Interactions, Interfaces, walks each node through the pipeline, and validates the whole walk before writing anything. Target: ready | in-progress | in-review | ship.

change.description: The change id walked by scope "change"; with node_id + new_status, which open revision of the node moves (optional when it has at most one).

nodes.description: Scope "change" only: walk just these members of the change (each must be a member); the others stay where they are. Works with dry_run, skip_review, skip_blocked.

skip_review.description: Scoped walk to ship only: allow moving nodes that are not in-review yet. Each still passes the in-review gate; the result lists skipped_review.

skip_blocked.description: Scoped walk only: walk every node whose whole walk passes, leave each blocked node where it is (no partial steps), and list them in blocked ({ node_id, step, reason }). Blocked when no node can move.

dry_run.description: Validate and return the plan and the first Blocked reason without writing anything (with skip_blocked: the walkable plan and every blocked node).

revisions.description: One revision. Server orders Foundations, Interactions, Interfaces, then Bugs, and tries every item (a Blocked item stays put, the rest move). Mutually exclusive with node_id and new_status.

node_id.description: Node to transition.

change.description: Which open revision of a shipped node moves; optional when it has at most one. One node may appear once per change.

Runs every idempotent migration and stamps mindplan/version.json; returns { from_level, to_level, changed_files, hook?, migrations, leftovers, pointer_outdated, pointer, guide }: delete the leftovers and follow the guide. instructions: Before answering any questions or writing any code for this project, call get_project and follow the playbook, description, and rules it returns. The graph exists so the product can grow by addition: the next feature should be new nodes and links, not reopened shipped ones. A new behavior is a new node. Before you claim the files of a new feature, create its node (Interaction, Interface, or Foundation) and link it; when a change alters what existing nodes describe, update those nodes. Write mindplan/ only through these tools (reading its files directly is fine). Before handing work off, run_check must pass.
